title: California Hospital Fair Pricing Act (Health and Safety Code 127400-127446)
asOf: Text as amended by AB 2297, effective 2025-01-01

rules.title: Who qualifies: self-pay or high medical costs, income at or under 400% FPL
rules.plain: If you're uninsured (or your out-of-pocket costs are high) and your family income is at or under 400% of the poverty line, California hospitals must offer you discounted payment or charity care.
rules.quote: A patient who has a family income that does not exceed 400 percent of the federal poverty level.
rules.notes: High medical costs: out-of-pocket costs at the hospital over 10% of family income (127400(g)). Rural hospitals may set lower limits (127405(a)(2)).

rules.title: Charge cap: what Medicare or Medi-Cal would pay
rules.plain: If you qualify, the hospital can only expect what Medicare or Medi-Cal would pay for your care, whichever is more.
rules.quote: from Medicare or Medi-Cal, whichever is greater

rules.title: No deadline to apply, assets not counted
rules.plain: There's no deadline to apply, the hospital can't count your savings, and pay stubs or a tax return are enough proof of income.
rules.quote: A hospital shall not impose time limits for applying for charity care or discounted payments

rules.title: Interest-free payment plan, at most 10% of monthly income
rules.plain: If you qualify, you can pay over time with no interest. If you can't agree on a plan, payments are capped at 10% of your monthly family income after essential expenses.

rules.title: No credit reporting; no lawsuit before 180 days
rules.plain: California hospitals and their collectors can't report your hospital debt to credit bureaus, can't sue within 180 days of the first bill, and can't garnish wages or put liens on your home if you qualify for assistance.
rules.quote: Report adverse information to a consumer credit reporting agency.
